what: Coca-Cola FEMSA is the largest Coca-Cola bottler in the world by volume. It makes and distributes Coca-Cola products across Mexico, Brazil, Guatemala, Colombia and several other Latin American countries.
customers: Supermarkets, small neighbourhood shops, restaurants and street vendors across Latin America.
money: bottling and distribution in Mexico, Guatemala, Costa Rica and others
moat: Exclusive bottling territories for the world's best-known drinks brands, with a distribution network that reaches millions of tiny shops competitors cannot serve economically.
risks: Sugar taxes and packaging rules are tightening across Latin America
Currency devaluation in Argentina and Brazil distorts reported results
Mexican consumer spending depends on remittances and employment
opportunities: Revenue grew about 14% last year and about 13% a year over three years
Per-person consumption in several of its markets is still rising
A dividend yield above 3% with reliable cash generation
watch: Volume growth by country and revenue per unit case.
